> **Draft — direction change pending team sign-off.** Reverses the round-2 decision that "the CLI is the single source of truth" for cost. Opening as a draft so it can be reviewed alongside #1702 before committing to the reversal. Pairs with entirehq/entire-api (platform computes cost).

## What

The CLI stops **persisting** cost into checkpoint metadata. It keeps persisting the token facts the platform prices from (`model_usage` with all four token fields per model + model id, flat token counts, model, api-call counts). Cost is now shown only as a clearly-labeled **local estimate** in the token commands.

## Why

Per team discussion (Dipree): don't store cost in the CLI — the platform can pull fresh pricing far faster (no CLI release to fix a rate or add a model). The CLI's job narrows to capturing the facts only it can see; the platform (entire-api) owns pricing and the authoritative cost.

## How

- A single choke point — `Metadata.WithoutCost()` / `CheckpointSummary.WithoutCost()` — applied at all six checkpoint-metadata marshal sites (branch + refs backends). It clears `cost_usd`/`cost_source` at every level (flat, subagent subtree, each per-model bucket) while preserving the four token fields, model ids, and counts.
- The in-memory compute path is intentionally **kept** — condensation's model-recovery rebucketing keys on `CostUSD == nil`, so removing it would change when `model_usage` is rebucketed. Only what's written to disk drops cost.
- Token commands (`entire session tokens`, `entire checkpoint tokens [--compare]`, `entire tokens profile`) recompute a local estimate on the fly via `agent.EstimateCost` from the persisted tokens + `model_usage`, labeled `$X (estimated locally)` with a note that the authoritative cost lives on the platform. Unknown model → no cost line (never `$0`). The `pricing/` package is retained for this local display.

## Supersedes

Supersedes #1702 (which computed and stored cost in the CLI). This branch is #1702 **plus** the two reduction commits on top.

## Testing

- `gofmt`/`mise run lint` clean; `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/... ./api/checkpoint/...` green.
- `TestWriteCommitted_DoesNotPersistCost`: a checkpoint with cost + subagents + per-model buckets round-trips with token counts / model ids / subagent counts intact and cost nil/empty at every level.
- Updated condensation test proves persisted `model_usage` is bucketed under the recovered model with token counts, but no cost.
- Display tests: token commands still render a cost line, computed live, labeled as a local estimate.

## Note for review

Backfill/summary rewrites now also strip cost from any **legacy** checkpoint they rewrite (cost written by an older CLI is cleared on the next attribution/summary backfill). Consistent with "the CLI does not persist cost" — flagging to confirm it's intended.

## Follow-up

If the team decides the CLI should drop cost **display** entirely too, the `pricing/` package + the cost fields/machinery could be removed (larger blast radius — condensation's model-recovery currently rides on the cost path; would need re-expressing as a pure model-signal). Not done here.

{"additions":6356,"author":{"is_bot":true,"login":"app/entire"},"baseRefName":"main","body":"**Trail:** https://entire.io/gh/entirehq/entire-api/trails/298

> **Draft — direction change pending team sign-off.** This reverses the round-2 decision that "the CLI is the single source of truth and the server never estimates." Opening as a draft so the new design can be reviewed side-by-side with #261 before we commit to the reversal.

## What

entire-api computes checkpoint/session/per-model cost **itself**, at ingest, from the `model_usage` token breakdown it already ingests — and ignores any cost the CLI supplies. Pairs with the CLI change in entireio/cli (CLI stops storing cost).

## Why

Per team discussion (Dipree): cost shouldn't be stored in the CLI; the platform can pull fresh pricing far faster (no CLI release to correct a rate or add a model). Splitting the feature by ownership: the CLI captures the facts only it can see (tokens + model + fast/api-usage); the platform owns pricing and the authoritative cost.

## How

- New `internal/pricing/` — the CLI's audited pricing engine ported verbatim (byte-identical rate tables for anthropic/openai/google/cursor, id-spelling resolution incl. Bedrock/Vertex/tier variants, Anthropic cache multipliers 0.1×/1.25×). Own `Usage` type; no cross-repo dep. Ported unit tests included.
- `internal/ingest/cost.go` `estimateCost` + `parseSession`/`buildCheckpointRow`: each `model_usage` bucket is priced from its four token fields (input/cache-creation/cache-read/output), summed to the checkpoint/session cost, `cost_source = estimated`. Unknown model → nil (never a guess). The CLI-supplied `cost_usd` is **ignored entirely**; the unpriceable-root fallback was removed (nil, never a stale number).
- Reuses the existing cost columns + aggregation panels unchanged. Raw token buckets stay stored, so a Phase-3 re-price job can recompute when rates change without re-ingesting.

## Supersedes

Supersedes #261 (which ingested and stored the CLI's cost). This branch is #261's ingestion/panels/migrations **plus** the two server-compute commits on top.

## Testing

- `go build`/`vet`/`gofmt`/`mise run lint` clean; unit (pricing 64, ingest tests) + `test:integration` (16 cost tests) + `test:pipeline` green (throwaway PG+NATS).
- Math verified: a claude-opus-4-8 bucket (200k in / 50k out / 1M cache-read / 100k cache-write) → **$3.375000**, exact vs hand math and vs `pricing.Estimate`.
- **Live E2E (R2):** the real ingest code, driven on a real new-CLI checkpoint (no stored cost) against live Postgres, computed **$0.0800115** (= rate math); a planted CLI cost of `999.99` was ignored; surfaced in Postgres (`0.080012`) and the HTTP detail DTO.
- **Live E2E (R1 — full transport, confirmed):** real `git push` → entiredb ref → NATS `repo_refs_v1` → `run:repo` ingest (computes cost) → Postgres → **authed** `GET /v1/repos/{id}/overview/checkpoint-metrics` returned `{"cost_usd":0.080012,"cost_source":"estimated",...}` (unauthed → 401). The pushed checkpoint carried `model_usage` and **no cost field**, so the platform computed the whole figure from scratch — the definitive proof that cost is platform-owned.

## Known findings (for review)

- **Dual precision in one response:** checkpoint `cost_usd` is `NUMERIC(14,6)` (`0.080012`) while per-model JSONB keeps full float (`0.0800115`) — summing sessions ≠ top-level (sub-cent). Decide whether to align.
- **Cost is load-bearing on `model_usage[].model`:** an ingested path with aggregate tokens but no resolvable `model_usage` model yields nil cost (the old CLI-computes design was more forgiving). Confirm every cost-bearing agent emits `model_usage`.

## Follow-ups

Phase 3: server-side live pricing pull (a pricing git repo + `git pull`, per jdx, is lighter than a JSON API) + a re-price job over the stored token buckets. No pricing-source live-refresh in this PR (embedded table only).


---

## Review follow-up (2026-07-16 update)

**Merged `main`** (through #306). One conflict, in `internal/httpapi/transcript.go`: kept the platform-computed cost fields on the session envelope while adopting main's `codeRepoID`/`sessionID` parameterization of `buildSessionTranscript`.

**Migration renumber.** `main` grew the repo-store migrations to 050 (…`049_trail_attachments_dimensions`, `050_session_shares_share_id`), colliding with this branch's cost migration at 049. Renumbered it to **`051_checkpoint_session_cost.sql`** — the next free version after main's max (046 stays permanently skipped) — and updated the three comment references. goose derives each version from the filename prefix and rejects duplicate versions, so the two version-049 files would otherwise fail provider construction. The user-store cost migration stays at `009_my_activity_cost.sql` (main's user-store max is 008, no collision). `mise run test:pipeline` applies the full 001→051 chain and the cost pipeline tests (`…MeSessionsCost`, `…MeCheckpointsCost`, `…ConsumerSanitizesRogueCost`, `…ProjectSpendZeroCosted`) pass, proving the renumber. _Note: main now documents a UTC-timestamp migration convention (CONTRIBUTING.md, COR incident). I kept an integer (051) to match main's de-facto `048/049/050` sequence; happy to re-stamp to a timestamp if the team prefers, since it would permanently end this migration's recurring renumber._

**Pricing freshness (addresses the "so they don't go stale" review point).** Kept the raw `internal/pricing/models/*.json`, but added a discoverable, runnable updater:

- `mise run pricing:check` — compares every tracked model against an upstream machine-readable source (LiteLLM's `model_prices_and_context_window.json` by default; any LiteLLM-schema file or URL via `-source`, e.g. a cached copy for offline/CI) and reports per-field drift. Non-zero exit on drift, so it can gate. It intentionally does **not** reuse the pricing engine's broad alias globs for matching, so a sibling like `gpt-5-mini` can't be mistaken for `gpt-5`.
- `mise run pricing:update` — `-write`: applies the matchable updates in place and bumps `effective_date`. Models with no confident upstream match (our newer/internal ids: `claude-opus-4-8`, `gpt-5.5`, `claude-fable-5`, `gemini-3-pro`, `composer-2`, …) are listed as **manually maintained** and are never guessed at or erased.
- Provenance lives in `internal/pricing/models/SOURCE.md`, with a pointer from `doc.go`. This is a stopgap; the phase-3 server-side live refresh (the CLI's remote-refresh, ported) supersedes it.

<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Summary

Stands up `GET /pricing/v1/models.json` — the endpoint the CLI's pricing-refresh mechanism (entireio/cli#1763) already expects at `https://entire.io/pricing/v1/models.json` but which doesn't exist anywhere yet, so the CLI currently degrades silently to its embedded pricing snapshot.

This is the "Pi method" approach discussed in the team Slack thread on entirehq/entire-api#299 / entireio/cli#1763: an embedded baseline shipped with the CLI, plus a background overlay refreshed from our own hosted catalog (rather than depending on Pi/pi.dev directly), sourced the same way Pi sources theirs — from `models.dev`.

- Route registered on the `entire-io-api` Worker (exact-path carve-out on the `entire.io` zone, same mechanism as the existing `/auth/*`, `/api/v1/*`, `/.well-known/entire-api.json` carve-outs — Cloudflare route matching prefers the more specific pattern over the frontend Worker's `entire.io/*` catch-all, verified against Cloudflare's documented routing precedence).
- `Content-Type: application/json`, content-hash `ETag`, real `304` on matching `If-None-Match`, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600`, no auth required.
- Generator (`api/scripts/generate-pricing-catalog.ts`) pulls live from `models.dev/api.json`, filters to first-party model vendors only (anthropic, openai, google, xai, meta, mistral, cohere, deepseek, and a few others), and hard-fails (throws) on any duplicate model id surviving the filter — models.dev lists many of the same model ids under dozens of reseller/aggregator provider keys at different prices, so an unfiltered flatten would hand the CLI wrong-provider, wrong-price data.
- `effective_date` is stamped at ingest time (today), not copied from models.dev's own `last_updated` field — that field isn't a reliable price-change signal (bumped by any edit to hand-authored provider files, not just price edits).
- Committed catalog: 218 models, 57 KB (well under the CLI's 1 MiB fetch cap).

**Known limitation, intentionally left as follow-up**: regeneration is manual (`pnpm generate:pricing-catalog`), not wired into CI/build yet — the team hasn't settled on an automated refresh cadence/ownership model for this.

## Test plan
- [x] Full `vitest.unit.config.ts` suite green (204 files / 4007 tests)
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean, `oxlint` clean
- [x] Route tested end-to-end through the real Hono app (200 + schema + ETag + genuine 304)
- [x] Generator tested for: aggregator-provider exclusion, zero-duplicate-id invariant, correct `claude-sonnet-4-6` → `anthropic` resolution
- [x] Verified end-to-end against the real `entire` CLI binary: fetched over HTTP, parsed, accepted all 218 entries with zero rejections","changedFiles":10,"deletions":0,"headRefName":"feat/pricing-catalog-endpoint","state":"OPEN","title":"feat(pricing): add /pricing/v1/models.json catalog endpoint","url":"https://github.com/entirehq/entire.io/pull/3643"}

import { Hono } from "hono"
import { etag } from "hono/etag"

import type { Env, Variables } from "../env"
import pricingCatalog from "../lib/pricing/pricing-models.json"

/**
 * Public, unauthenticated pricing catalog feed.
 *
 * Serves the committed src/lib/pricing/pricing-models.json (built from
 * models.dev by scripts/generate-pricing-catalog.ts) at GET /pricing/v1/models.json.
 * This is what entireio/cli's daily pricing-refresh mechanism
 * (cmd/entire/cli/pricing/remote.go, PR #1763) polls, ETag-conditionally, so
 * the CLI's embedded model pricing never goes stale without a release.
 *
 * Mounted directly on the top-level app (see ../app.ts), NOT under /api/v1 —
 * this must resolve at the bare-domain path the CLI hits
 * (https://entire.io/pricing/v1/models.json), and it has no auth/DB/KV
 * dependency, so it skips the v1 sub-app's no-store/auth machinery entirely.
 * wrangler.jsonc carves an exact route for this path out of the frontend
 * worker's `entire.io/*` catch-all, the same way /auth/*, /api/v1/*, and
 * /.well-known/entire-api.json already are.
 *
 * LIMITATION: regeneration is manual/on-demand only (`pnpm --filter
 * entire-api run generate:pricing-catalog`, committed by hand) — there is no
 * CI cron/action wiring this up yet. That's an intentional follow-up the team
 * hasn't decided on; this route always serves whatever was last committed.
 */
export const pricingRoutes = new Hono<{ Bindings: Env; Variables: Variables }>()

pricingRoutes.get("/v1/models.json", etag(), (c) => {
  // Safe to cache aggressively at the edge: this response only changes when
  // the generator is rerun and recommitted, and the etag() middleware above
  // still recomputes a fresh ETag from the served body on every regeneration
  // (and every deploy), so a regen is never masked by a stale edge cache
  // beyond max-age.
  c.header("Cache-Control", "public, max-age=3600")
  return c.json(pricingCatalog)
})

# Pricing source & provenance

These JSON files are the **hand-maintained** per-model token rates the platform
uses to estimate checkpoint/session cost (see `internal/pricing/doc.go`). Rates

  (Anthropic / OpenAI / Google / Cursor pricing pages).
- **Cross-check / drift source:** [LiteLLM's
  `model_prices_and_context_window.json`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/main/model_prices_and_context_window.json)
  — a comprehensive, machine-readable table of public model prices. LiteLLM
  stores per-*token* costs; we store per-*MTok*, so a rate is `× 1e6`.
  ([OpenRouter's `/api/v1/models`](https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models) is a
  viable secondary source in the same spirit.)

## Keep them fresh — don't let them rot

```sh
mise run pricing:check     # read-only: report drift vs upstream (non-zero exit on drift)
mise run pricing:update    # apply the matchable updates in place, then review the diff
```

Both wrap `go run ./internal/pricing/pricingcheck`. `pricing:check` compares
every model we track against upstream and prints `ok` / `DRIFT` per model plus a
list of the manually-maintained ones; `pricing:update` (`-write`) rewrites the
matchable rates and bumps their `effective_date`. Run `check` periodically (e.g.
before a release) so a silent provider price change gets caught.

Point either at an offline/cached copy with `-- -source ./litellm.json`.

## Manually maintained (no upstream match)

Newer or internal model ids are **not** present in public pricing tables and are
maintained by hand — the updater lists them and **never guesses or erases**
them. This currently covers ids such as `claude-opus-4-8`, `claude-fable-5`,
`claude-mythos-5`, `gpt-5.5`, the `gpt-5.6-*` family, `gemini-3-pro`, and the
`composer-2*` (Cursor) models. Run `mise run pricing:check` for the exact,
current partition of matched vs. manually-maintained.

When you add such a model, set its rate from the provider's pricing page and
record the date in `effective_date`.

## Note: this is a stopgap

Drift detection here is a runnable command, not a live sync. Phase 3 will add the
server-side equivalent of the CLI's live remote-pricing refresh (a pulled pricing
source + a re-price job over the stored token buckets); see the `TODO(phase3)`
notes in `doc.go`, `table.go`, and `internal/ingest/cost.go`.

-- +goose Up
-- Checkpoint / session cost, threaded from the CLI's metadata.json token_usage
-- blocks (root summary + per-session), the twin of the existing token columns.
-- cost_usd is NUMERIC(14,6) (money, not a count) and NULLABLE — absence means
-- the payload reported no cost (an old checkpoint predating cost capture), which
-- is DISTINCT from a real 0.00, so there is no DEFAULT. cost_source records how
-- the cost was derived ('reported' — the cost the CLI computed at session time,
-- against the rates then in force, and persisted into the metadata; 'estimated' —
-- derived here from the token breakdown when the payload carried none; or 'mixed'
-- when a checkpoint/session aggregates both); NULL when no cost was carried. The CHECK pins the vocabulary so a bad ingest can't smuggle
-- an unknown source in. Read/aggregate paths land in a later change; this only
-- widens the write side.
--
-- The CHECK is added NOT VALID: cost_source is a brand-new column, so every
-- existing row is NULL and trivially satisfies it — there is nothing to validate,
-- and NOT VALID skips the full-table scan that a plain ADD CONSTRAINT would run
-- under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE (which would stall ingestion on a large, live checkpoints/
-- sessions table). NOT VALID still ENFORCES the constraint on every new insert /
-- update (the poison-value protection), so no follow-up VALIDATE is required.
SET search_path TO repo, public;

ALTER TABLE checkpoints
    ADD COLUMN cost_usd NUMERIC(14,6),
    ADD COLUMN cost_source TEXT,
    ADD CONSTRAINT checkpoints_cost_source_check
        CHECK (cost_source IS NULL OR cost_source IN ('reported', 'estimated', 'mixed')) NOT VALID;

ALTER TABLE sessions
    ADD COLUMN cost_usd NUMERIC(14,6),
    ADD COLUMN cost_source TEXT,
    ADD CONSTRAINT sessions_cost_source_check
        CHECK (cost_source IS NULL OR cost_source IN ('reported', 'estimated', 'mixed')) NOT VALID;

-- +goose Down
SET search_path TO repo, public;

ALTER TABLE sessions
    DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS sessions_cost_source_check,
    DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS cost_source,
    DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS cost_usd;

ALTER TABLE checkpoints
    DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS checkpoints_cost_source_check,
    DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS cost_source,
    DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS cost_usd;

content.text:
I read all three at head (not just the diffs) and cross-checked them against each other. The headline is a process problem, and one concrete cross-repo bug.

## 1. All three descriptions describe a design that was reversed. Two are inverted.

The "platform owns cost" direction was flipped back to "CLI owns cost" — on both sides — but neither title nor body was updated.

**cli#1763** says it stops persisting cost via a `WithoutCost()` choke point, verified by `TestWriteCommitted_DoesNotPersistCost`. At head: commit `67953777 refactor(cost): persist cost in checkpoint metadata again`; `WithoutCost` does not exist anywhere in the branch; the test is `TestWriteCommitted_PersistsCost`; and `api/checkpoint/metadata.go:396` reads *"Cost is persisted deliberately… Writers persist Metadata as-is — nothing strips cost."*

**entire-api#299** says "the CLI-supplied `cost_usd` is **ignored entirely**." At head, `internal/ingest/cost.go` `bucketCost` does the opposite — CLI cost wins, server estimate is the fallback (`aa487812`, `ff1d3610`, both 2026-08-10).

Two consequences worth acting on:

- **jagregory's approval on #299 is dated 2026-07-16 — 25 days before the reversal.** It approved "platform computes cost." Nobody has signed off on what's on the branch.
- All three are **out of draft** while their bodies still say *"Draft — direction change pending team sign-off."*

Also stale in #299: the entire "renumbered to 051" paragraph (migrations are correctly UTC-timestamped now — `20260817182746` / `20260810140753`, both above main's max in their stores; that part is clean), and the "cost is load-bearing on `model_usage[].model`" known finding, which the reported-cost path now mitigates.

## 2. Real bug: entire.io's catalog silently disables the CLI's 2× 1-hour cache-write pricing

This one only shows up when you read the three together.

`cmd/entire/cli/pricing/table.go` `Estimate` applies the 2.0× Anthropic 1h-TTL premium **only when the model omits an explicit cache-write rate**:

```go
if r.CacheWritePerMTok != nil { cwRate = *r.CacheWritePerMTok }
cw1hRate := cwRate
if isAnthropic && r.CacheWritePerMTok == nil { cw1hRate = 2.0 * r.InputPerMTok }
```

All **20** CLI embedded Anthropic entries deliberately leave `cache_read_per_mtok`/`cache_write_per_mtok` null so the 0.1×/1.25×/2.0× multipliers apply. All **13** Anthropic entries in entire.io's generated catalog supply explicit values (models.dev carries them) — the 5-minute rates. `Table.add` inherits cache rates only when the incoming ones are nil, so the remote entry wins outright.

Net for `claude-opus-4-8` ($5/MTok input) with `pricing.remote: true`: 1-hour cache writes bill at **$6.25/MTok instead of $10.00/MTok — a 37.5% undercount** on that component. It silently reverts cli#1763's own commit `d0bc7afb fix(cost): price 1-hour-TTL cache writes at 2x`, and because the platform now *trusts* the CLI's number, the undercount becomes the stored cost of record.

Latent today (`pricing.remote` defaults false, and the refresh spawn is correctly gated on it in `pricing_refresh.go:52` — no unsolicited traffic, that part is well done), but making that opt-in useful is the whole point of #3643.

Fix: have the generator emit `cache_write_per_mtok: null` for `provider === "anthropic"` — one line, works with already-shipped CLIs. Longer term add `cache_write_1h_per_mtok` to the schema and teach the CLI to read it. Note the existing compat test ("accepted all 218 entries with zero rejections") checks *parseability*, not that the merged table prices the same; a golden-cost assertion would have caught this.

## 3. Three pricing tables, three refresh mechanisms, nothing reconciling them

- CLI `cmd/entire/cli/pricing/models/*.json` — hand-edited.
- entire-api `internal/pricing/models/*.json` — I hashed all four files; **byte-identical to the CLI's today**. Drift-checked against **LiteLLM** via `mise run pricing:check`.
- entire.io `/pricing/v1/models.json` — generated from **models.dev**, manual regen.

Nothing keeps the first two identical, and nothing points the second at the third. They already disagree in principle: entire-api's `SOURCE.md` lists `claude-opus-4-8` as "manually maintained, no upstream match," while entire.io's models.dev-derived catalog carries it (at 5/25, matching).

Bounded today — the server estimate is only a fallback. But the `TODO(phase3)` re-price job in `ingest/cost.go` would recompute stored buckets with entire-api's table, which is not the table the CLI priced with. Cheapest immediate guard: a CI check that the two embedded dirs stay byte-identical. Better: entire-api consumes the same `/pricing/v1/models.json`.

## 4. Post-reversal, the CLI stores the authoritative cost and then refuses to show it

`session_tokens.go:283` `applyLocalCostEstimate` *"replaces a rendered usage's cost with a LOCAL, on-the-fly estimate… at current rates"* — and `checkpoint_tokens.go:384` is explicit: *"at current rates, not read from the buckets' persisted spend-time cost."*

The user-facing note (`session_tokens.go:460`) still says *"Cost is a local estimate at current rates; the authoritative cost is computed on the Entire platform."* That was true under the reverted design. Now the platform copies the CLI's stored number — so the CLI points users elsewhere for a value it wrote itself and declined to display. `entire checkpoint tokens` will drift from the stored cost the moment a rate changes or the remote overlay lands, with a note that explains the difference backwards.

The live-session consistency rationale is sound; render the persisted cost for checkpointed usage, keep the estimate for live state, rewrite the note.

## 5. Smaller

- **Dual precision** (still real, still unresolved): `checkpoints.cost_usd` is `NUMERIC(14,6)` while per-model JSONB keeps full float — summing sessions ≠ top level, sub-cent. Pick one.
- **Remote entries carry `aliases: []`.** Fine for ids already embedded (`Table.add` inherits). But the ~200 *new* models the catalog adds get no aliases, so dated/Bedrock/Vertex spellings won't resolve — blunting "add a model without a CLI release" for exactly the models it's meant to cover.

- **2s total fetch budget** against a Cloudflare Worker, and every failure bumps `FetchedAt` — one cold-start timeout costs a full day of staleness. Degrades safely; consider not resetting the clock on a transport error.
- **#3643's generator is manual-only.** With the CLI polling daily against a 24h cache, a stale committed catalog is invisible. A CI cron behind the existing sanity gates would close it.

The risk here is almost entirely that the paper trail describes a different system than the code does, and the one place that mismatch has already produced a live defect is the Anthropic cache-rate collision in §2.

Suggested fix: pick one precision and apply it at the boundary. Rounding each bucket to 6dp before it goes into the JSONB (so the parts sum to the whole) is the cheaper of the two; the alternative is widening the column and rendering full precision everywhere.

  -m 'Manual-only catalog regeneration makes staleness invisible

api/package.json wires generate:pricing-catalog as an on-demand script; nothing runs it in CI. The route serves whatever api/src/lib/pricing/pricing-models.json was last committed, and the PR notes this as an intentional follow-up.

Why it matters more than it looks: the consumer side is fully automatic and fully silent. The CLI polls once per 24h with an ETag, and a matching ETag is a 304 that the CLI records as refreshOutcomeNotModified -- indistinguishable from "upstream confirmed nothing changed". So a catalog that has not been regenerated in months reports as healthy at every layer: 200/304 from the edge, a fresh FetchedAt in the CLI cache, and every entry stamped with an effective_date that reflects the last GENERATION, not the last verification.

That inverts the stated purpose ("so the CLI embedded model pricing never goes stale without a release"): the mechanism removes the release requirement but replaces it with an unmonitored manual step, and removes the signal that the step was skipped.

Suggested fix: a scheduled CI job that runs the generator and opens a PR on diff. The existing guards make this safe to automate -- assertSaneModelsDevPayload, assertSaneCatalog, and assertNoDuplicateModelIds all throw rather than writing a degraded catalog, so a bad upstream fails the job instead of shipping. Failing that, surface generation age (e.g. a generated_at field the CLI can log) so staleness is at least observable.' 2>&1 | grep -E '"severity"' | head -2

fix(cost): resolve trail-review findings on 1h cache-write, checkpoint cost display, and pricing staleness

Three findings from the trail review (#865):

High: a remote pricing catalog entry that supplies only the 5-minute
Anthropic cache-write rate silently disabled the 2x 1-hour-TTL premium,
because Estimate only applied the 2x multiplier when CacheWritePerMTok
was nil. The two TTLs are independent multiples of input, not one
derived from the other, so an Anthropic entry now defaults the 1h rate
to 2x input regardless of whether a 5-minute rate is set. Add
CacheWrite1hPerMTok so a source that knows the real 1h rate can still
say so explicitly.

Medium: checkpoint/profile token commands discarded the checkpoint's
persisted spend-time cost and re-estimated at today's rates for
display, even though the platform now trusts and stores the CLI's
reported cost. entire checkpoint tokens / entire tokens profile now
render the persisted cost_usd/cost_source when one exists, falling
back to a local estimate only for checkpoints written before cost
persistence existed. localCostEstimateNote no longer claims the
platform computes its own authoritative cost, and only prints for an
actual local estimate.

Low: a transport-level pricing-fetch failure (timeout, dial error,
connection dropped mid-read) bumped FetchedAt the same as a real
response from the source, blocking retry for a full 24h over one slow
request. Such a failure now backs off only transportRetryBackoff (1h)
instead of the full remoteRefreshInterval.

content.text:
All three of my CLI findings were fixed overnight, and your Slack direction was adopted wholesale.

## What moved

**Item 3 landed as an architecture change.** Commit `42c3256f feat(pricing): add pricing:sync to mirror entire-api's canonical catalog` — entire-api is now the source of truth (`internal/httpapi/pricing_catalog.go`), the CLI's embedded table became a release-time export of it, and entire.io's route is now a **proxy** (`fetch(upstreamURL)`) instead of a committed JSON. The models.dev generator script is gone. The commit message cites the 1h cache-write bug by name as the motivating example.

**Item 2 (High) — fixed, and fixed the better way.** `Estimate` now applies the 2× Anthropic 1h multiplier independent of whether a 5-minute rate is set, plus a new `CacheWrite1hPerMTok` for sources that know the real rate:
```go
cw1hRate := cwRate
if isAnthropic { cw1hRate = AnthropicCacheWrite1hMultiplier * r.InputPerMTok }
if r.CacheWrite1hPerMTok != nil { cw1hRate = *r.CacheWrite1hPerMTok }
```

**Item 4 (Medium) — fixed.** `applyCheckpointCost` now renders the persisted spend-time cost, falling back to a local estimate only for pre-persistence checkpoints. The note is rewritten: *"Cost is a local estimate at current rates for usage that has no persisted spend-time cost yet."*

**Item 5a (Low) — fixed.** `transportRetryBackoff = time.Hour` for transport failures, vs the full 24h for a real non-200.

## Still open

**PR titles and bodies are unchanged.** cli#1763 still reads *"CLI stops storing cost; platform owns it."* Item 1 hasn't been actioned.

**My two entire-api findings** (dual precision, subagent fallback) are untouched.

**My two entire.io findings are now moot** — the aliases problem is solved incidentally, since entire-api serves `pricing.ModelRate` straight from the hand-curated tables with alias sets intact rather than models.dev entries with `aliases: []`. The manual-regeneration finding described a generator that no longer exists; the underlying freshness question just moved to entire-api, where the table is still hand-maintained with a LiteLLM drift check.

## One thing worth knowing about the trail

All seven of my findings are marked **`stale`**, because commits landed after I filed them. `entire trail finding list` defaults to `--freshness current`, so **the default view of trail 865 shows only one finding** — a new High on `remote.go:320` filed overnight by someone else. Mine are invisible without `--freshness any`. Same on the other two trails. If the team is working from the dashboard, the fixed ones reading as stale-open is noise, and the genuinely-unaddressed entire-api ones are hidden.

Want me to resolve the three fixed CLI findings and dismiss the two obsolete entire.io ones? That'd leave the two real entire-api items plus whatever's freshly filed. I haven't touched them since you didn't ask.

result.output:
fix(cost): document legacy subagent-token scope, round bucket costs to column precision

Two findings from the trail review (#298), both low severity:

Legacy fallback (no model_usage on the checkpoint) prices only the flat
parent token fields, excluding a subagent subtree the CLI's TokenUsage
type carries but this repo's tokenUsage does not model. This is
deliberate, not an oversight: every checkpoint carrying model_usage
already captures subagent tokens via the CLI's dispatcher remainder
bucket, so the gap only touches checkpoints written before both cost
persistence and model_usage existed. Documented at both the struct and
the else-branch rather than changed, per the finding's own scope
assessment.

Per-model bucket costs were stored in the sessions JSONB at full
float64 precision while checkpoints.cost_usd/sessions.cost_usd are
NUMERIC(14,6) — so a consumer summing the JSONB breakdown could get a
different number than the top-level column by sub-cent amounts.
bucketCost now rounds to the column scale (store.RoundCostUSD) at the
single choke point every caller shares, so the per-bucket JSONB values
and the totals summed from them agree with each other and with what
Postgres stores.

Entire-Checkpoint: 630a6d8a2ad1

content.text:
Substantial movement on all three. Every one of my seven findings is now addressed, and your item-3 direction landed across all three repos.

## Fixed since Monday

**All 3 CLI findings** (`10a8cb8a`) — the 1h cache-write fix is better than what I suggested: the 2× premium is now an independent multiple of input rather than conditional on the 5-minute rate being absent, plus a new `CacheWrite1hPerMTok` escape hatch. Checkpoint commands render the persisted cost; the note is rewritten. Transport failures back off 1h instead of 24h.

**Both entire-api findings** (`cafb8fb1`) — subagent scope documented at struct + else-branch rather than changed (correct call), and `store.RoundCostUSD` applied at the `bucketCost` choke point so the JSONB breakdown and the NUMERIC column agree.

**Both entire.io findings are moot** — the models.dev generator is gone entirely. Aliases now arrive intact because entire-api serves the hand-curated table.

## Your item 3 shipped, end to end

- **entire-api** — `internal/httpapi/pricing_catalog.go`, public unauthenticated `GET /api/v1/pricing/models.json`, documented as canonical.
- **CLI** — `pricingsync` release-time export, plus `f4bfbae9` weekly CI freshness gate alerting to Slack on drift. That commit reasons it out correctly: release.yml can't fetch live at build time without making tags non-reproducible, so "pull current state at release" has to mean keeping main fresh ahead of the tag.
- **entire.io** — proxy using the explicit Cloudflare Cache API (a reviewer caught that `Cache-Control` alone doesn't populate the edge cache), plus an immutable-headers crash fix on cache hit.

## Four things still want you

**1. Titles and bodies unchanged — day three.** cli#1763 still reads *"CLI stops storing cost; platform owns it."* It's now doubly wrong: the branch also grew an entire pricing-sync subsystem that the description doesn't mention at all.

**2. The deploy-order dependency is live.** `https://entire.io/pricing/v1/models.json` returns 404 right now. `28deb9f1` documents the dependency rather than resolving it. Merge order has to be entire-api → entire.io → CLI, or you ship a proxy with no upstream and a weekly CI job that alerts on a 502.

Worth verifying on staging rather than trusting the annotation: `/api/v1/*` currently 401s unknown paths, and the new route opts out of middleware at the huma layer. If platform auth sits *in front of* huma, the credential-less Worker proxy gets 401 → 502 and the chain is dead. The "Deliberately no Middlewares" comment asserts this works; nothing has exercised it yet.

**3. Six High CASING-001 findings on entire-api that should be dismissed, not fixed.** `cost_usd`, `cost_source`, `costed_checkpoint_count` flagged as camelCase violations — but every sibling field in those structs is snake_case (`is_private`, `session_count`, `input_tokens`), the code carries an explicit false-positive annotation with rationale, and commit `7ca77ac4` already adjudicated this exact set in an earlier round. Renaming would produce a mixed-casing wire and break entire.io's mirrored consumer. This is a re-raise loop burning review attention on a PR that's otherwise close.

**4. Other people's findings still open on the CLI trail** — 2 High (`remainderBucket` attribution at `manual_commit_git.go:154`, and `remote.go:320`), 1 Medium (`accumulateTokenUsage` never sums `CacheCreation1hTokens` — same 1h-token class as the bug that started this), 1 Low.

Also: my five substantive findings still show `open` despite being fixed, and everything on all three trails is now `stale`, so the default dashboard view hides most of it.

Want me to resolve the five that are genuinely fixed and dismiss the two moot entire.io ones? I'd leave the CASING-001 six alone unless you want me to dismiss those too — they're someone else's findings and that's a call I'd rather you make.
ok, can you look again at everything

9:This is the "Pi method" approach discussed in the team Slack thread on entirehq/entire-api#299 / entireio/cli#1763: an embedded baseline shipped with the CLI, plus a background overlay refreshed from our own hosted catalog (rather than depending on Pi/pi.dev directly), sourced the same way Pi sources theirs — from `models.dev`.
13:- Generator (`api/scripts/generate-pricing-catalog.ts`) pulls live from `models.dev/api.json`, filters to first-party model vendors only (anthropic, openai, google, xai, meta, mistral, cohere, deepseek, and a few others), and hard-fails (throws) on any duplicate model id surviving the filter — models.dev lists many of the same model ids under dozens of reseller/aggregator provider keys at different prices, so an unfiltered flatten would hand the CLI wrong-provider, wrong-price data.
14:- `effective_date` is stamped at ingest time (today), not copied from models.dev's own `last_updated` field — that field isn't a reliable price-change signal (bumped by any edit to hand-authored provider files, not just price edits).
15:- Committed catalog: 218 models, 57 KB (well under the CLI's 1 MiB fetch cap).
28:## Update (2026-08-18): repointed to proxy entire-api instead of its own generator
30:The design above (this repo's own `models.dev`-sourced generator, committing a static `pricing-models.json` snapshot) is superseded. Team direction (Soph): three independently-updated copies of "the same" pricing rates — this repo's snapshot, entire-api's `internal/pricing` (a byte-for-byte port of the CLI's table, added in entirehq/entire-api#299), and the CLI's own embedded table — is exactly how a real bug happened: the CLI's 1-hour Anthropic cache-write premium went silently missing on one of them, because a source that only knew the 5-minute rate looked identical to one that deliberately omitted it. entire-api becomes the sole source of truth; this repo and the CLI both mirror it instead of maintaining independent copies.
35:- Deleted the generator (`scripts/generate-pricing-catalog.ts`), its test, and the committed static catalog — no longer an independent copy to keep in sync. The "regeneration is manual, not wired into CI" limitation above is resolved by removal rather than automation: there's nothing left to regenerate here.
38:Test plan below reflects the original static-generator design; see the new commit for the proxy's own coverage (mocked upstream: success, unconfigured, unreachable, non-2xx, malformed JSON) — full `vitest.unit.config.ts` suite (203 files / 3968 tests) still green, `tsc --noEmit` and `oxlint` clean.

## Update (2026-08-18): direction reversed again, merged main, findings fixed

**Correction to the top of this description:** the CLI does **not** stop persisting cost — that direction (described in "What"/"How" above) was itself reversed by a later commit on this branch ("persist cost in checkpoint metadata again"). Current behavior: the CLI persists `cost_usd`/`cost_source` in checkpoint metadata at every level (session, subagent subtree, per-model bucket), computed with cache-accurate local pricing at spend time. The platform (entire-api, PR entirehq/entire-api#299) now trusts and stores that reported cost rather than re-deriving it, on the reasoning that only the CLI knows the rates actually in force when the tokens were spent.

**Merged `origin/main`** (263 commits). Two conflicts, both a shape where main and this branch had each added something the other lacked at the same seam:
- `types.AddTokenUsage` (main's new recursive token summer, which also added `CacheCreation1hTokens`) vs this branch's cost-aware `aggregateTokenUsage` — resolved by delegating token summation to `AddTokenUsage` and layering cost on top, so neither `CostUSD` summing nor the subagent-token recursion is lost.
- `manual_commit_condensation.go`'s model-backfill/reprice path vs main's `withSubagentTokensFrom` subagent-total fill — the reprice was overwriting the fill; fixed by carrying the subagent total across both of the reprice's call sites.

**Trail review findings addressed** (all three, [trail #865](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/865)):
- **High — remote pricing catalog silently disabled the 2x Anthropic 1h cache-write premium.** A remote catalog entry supplying only the 5-minute cache-write rate made `Estimate` skip the 1-hour-TTL 2x multiplier entirely (the multiplier only applied when no 5-minute rate was set). The two TTLs are independent multiples of the input rate, not one derived from the other — an Anthropic entry now defaults the 1-hour rate to 2x input regardless of whether a 5-minute rate is present. Added `CacheWrite1hPerMTok` so a source that knows the real 1-hour rate can still say so explicitly and override the default.
- **Medium — CLI persists the authoritative cost, then displays a re-estimate instead.** `entire checkpoint tokens` and `entire tokens profile` were discarding a checkpoint's persisted spend-time cost and recomputing at today's rates for display — drifting from both the stored value and what the platform now shows for the same checkpoint. They now render the persisted `cost_usd`/`cost_source` when one exists, falling back to a local estimate only for checkpoints written before cost persistence existed (`entire session tokens`, which has genuinely no persisted cost for live session state, is unchanged). `localCostEstimateNote` no longer claims platform authority backwards, and only prints for an actual local estimate.
- **Low — one slow pricing fetch cost a full day of staleness.** A transport-level failure (timeout, dial error, connection dropped mid-read) bumped the refresh cache's `FetchedAt` the same as a real response from the source, blocking retry for the full 24h refresh interval over a single slow request (e.g. a Worker cold start). Such a failure now backs off only 1 hour instead of the full interval.

`mise run check` (fmt, lint, unit, integration, Vogon canary) is green on the merged tree.

All done. Titles updated on both PRs and trails, five findings resolved, two dismissed — each with a reason recording what fixed it or why it's obsolete.

**New titles** (same text on PR and trail):
- cli#1763 — `feat(cost): persist spend-time cost in checkpoints, sync pricing from entire-api`
- api#299 — `feat(cost): trust CLI-reported cost with server-side fallback, serve the canonical pricing catalog`
- io#3643 — `feat(pricing): proxy entire-api's canonical catalog at /pricing/v1/models.json`

I left the `(supersedes #1702)` / `(supersedes #261)` suffixes on the PR titles and dropped them from the trail titles, matching what was already there.

---

## CASING-001

It's a convention check asserting that **all Entire-defined JSON fields must be camelCase**. Six instances fired on entire-api#299, all High, all on the new cost fields: `cost_usd`, `cost_source`, `costed_checkpoints`, `costed_checkpoint_count` in `me_types.go` and `teamtypes.go`. Each says the same thing — *"Rename to `costUsd`."*

**They're wrong here, and following them would break things.** Three reasons:

**The surrounding structs are uniformly snake_case.** The `me_types.go` struct that `cost_usd` lives in has `is_private`, `session_count`, `session_ids`, `dead_session_indices`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`. Renaming just the two cost fields produces a wire format that's snake_case everywhere except two keys — strictly worse than either convention applied consistently.

**These aren't Entire-defined fields in the sense the rule means.** This struct mirrors entire.io's existing user-checkpoint wire format. The casing is inherited from a consumer contract, not chosen here. That's exactly the carve-out the rule intends — hence the annotation already sitting in the code above the fields:

```go
// snake_case matches this entire.io-mirrored user-checkpoint wire
// (checkpoint_id, commit_sha, input_tokens, …) — CASING-001 false positive
// (see RepoCapabilities).
```

**It would be a breaking API change.** entire.io reads these keys. Renaming ships a silent break for any consumer not updated in the same deploy.

**The part worth your attention is that this is a re-raise.** Commit `7ca77ac4 docs(api): document snake_case cost JSON keys (CASING-001 false positive)` adjudicated this exact set in an earlier round — that's what added the annotation. The check fired again anyway on the same fields, at High. So the annotation isn't suppressing it.

That's the actual bug: whatever emits CASING-001 either doesn't read the false-positive marker, or the marker's format doesn't match what it looks for. Left alone, every future PR touching these structs re-raises six Highs, and the real signal gets trained out of people. Worth fixing at the check rather than dismissing the findings each round — dismissing them clears today's dashboard and guarantees the same six come back.

I haven't touched them, as agreed. If you want them dismissed I'd use one reason pointing at `7ca77ac4` and the annotation, so the next person sees it's the second time.

ok, so what do we do here, I feel adding new APIs that already violate what casing should be is something we should change but only if the whole endpoint is new, but that's not the case, we are adding fields to existing APIs that are already using a different casing?
Good question, and it's checkable. Let me verify each of the six against main.

content.text:
Your instinct is right, and checking it turned up something that changes the framing. Let me give you the facts first.

## All six are additive-to-existing — confirmed

| Location | Field(s) added | Pre-existing siblings on main |
|---|---|---|
| `me_types.go:207-208` | `cost_usd`, `cost_source` | `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `session_count`, `is_private` |
| `teamtypes.go:183-185` | `cost_usd`, `cost_source`, `costed_checkpoints` | `cache_read_tokens`, `active_days`, `first_activity` |
| `teamtypes.go:319` | `costed_checkpoint_count` | `checkpoint_count`, `avg_cost_per_checkpoint`, `since`, `until` |

Every one is a new field joining a struct that already exists on main and is uniformly snake_case. Not one is a new endpoint.

## But the rule as written doesn't say what I implied

I called these false positives, following the code's own annotations. Reading the actual rule, that's not right. `.entire/runners/api-design-rules.yaml`:

```yaml
- id: CASING-001
  level: MUST
  rule: All Entire-defined JSON field names are camelCase; externally
        standardized protocol documents use the field names prescribed
        by that protocol.
```

The only carve-out is external protocols — OIDC, JWK. **There is no exemption for "matches the endpoint it's joining."** So by the letter, these six are real violations that the codebase has been annotating as false positives. Substantively the annotations are right; formally they're asserting an exception the rule doesn't grant. One of them even argues "there is no camelCase API standard," which the rule file directly contradicts.

The codebase has two de facto conventions: reviews/changes surfaces are camelCase *per* CASING-001, while me/team surfaces are snake_case. Both cite the same rule.

## And the check is inverted

The genuinely-new endpoint in this PR — `GET /api/v1/pricing/models.json` — is **entirely snake_case**: `schema_version`, `input_per_mtok`, `cache_read_per_mtok`, `cache_write_1h_per_mtok`, `effective_date`. It was **not flagged at all**.

So the check fired six Highs on the additive cases that should match their neighbours, and stayed silent on the one brand-new public surface where camelCase would legitimately apply. Worth finding out why it was missed — the rule's signal targets OpenAPI `components.schemas`, so either the huma registration isn't landing in the scanned spec or the run predated that commit.

## What I'd do

**1. Amend CASING-001 rather than keep annotating.** Write your rule into it — new endpoints and new response shapes MUST be camelCase; fields added to an existing shape MUST match that shape's established casing. That converts six recurring Highs into a documented exception and stops the re-raise loop permanently. Case-by-case annotations demonstrably don't suppress it — `7ca77ac4` already tried.

**2. Decide the pricing catalog explicitly, and this week.** It's the one genuinely new public surface, so under both the written rule and your amendment it should be camelCase. The counter-argument is real: it's a `schema_version: 1` contract already implemented in three places — entire-api's serving struct, the CLI's `fileSchema`/`ModelRate`, entire.io's TS `PricingCatalog` — and the CLI's on-disk `models/*.json` files use the same keys.

My recommendation is to **keep snake_case and document it as a versioned cross-repo schema**, treating it like a wire format rather than an API response. But that's a judgment call, and it's time-sensitive: the endpoint 404s in production today because nothing is merged. Right now changing it is three coordinated edits. After it deploys and the CLI starts syncing from it, it's a `schema_version` bump across three repos.

**3. Dismiss the six with one reason pointing at the amendment**, once it's written — not before, or they come back.

Want me to draft the CASING-001 amendment text, or file the inverted-coverage problem as a finding on trail 298?

content.text:
**Roughly half a day**, and it's smaller than it looks because entire.io needs zero changes.

## Why entire.io is free

The proxy is field-agnostic — it parses to `unknown`, checks only that the body is syntactically valid JSON, re-serializes and caches:

```ts
let catalog: unknown
try { catalog = await upstream.json() } catch { ...502 }
const res = c.json(catalog)
```

And `api/src/lib/pricing/` was deleted entirely when `6925a088` removed the generator, so there's no typed `PricingCatalog` interface left in that repo. Whatever entire-api serves, entire.io passes through.

## The one design decision that sets the size

`pricing.ModelRate`'s tags are currently shared by **three** things: the HTTP wire, the embedded `models/*.json` build assets, and — critically — the user-facing `pricing.models` override block in `.entire/settings.json`.

So renaming the tags on `ModelRate` directly would silently break every user who has pricing overrides configured. That's not acceptable, which makes the answer straightforward: **camelCase the wire only, leave storage and config alone.** Add a DTO at the HTTP boundary. That's what `schema_version` was there for anyway.

## Scope under that split

**entire-api — ~1 file**
`pricing_catalog.go` gets a camelCase response DTO (`schemaVersion`, `inputPerMTok`, `cacheReadPerMTok`, `cacheWrite1hPerMTok`, `effectiveDate`, …) plus a mapper from `[]pricing.ModelRate`. ~40 lines and its test. `internal/pricing/`, the embedded JSON, and `pricingcheck` are all untouched.

**CLI — ~2 files, this is where the work is**
- `pricing/remote.go` currently unmarshals the fetched document straight into `fileSchema`, the same struct the embedded files use. That seam has to split: a camelCase remote shape plus a conversion into `[]ModelRate`. 6 key sites, and `remote_refresh_test.go` has 4 fixtures.
- `pricing/pricingsync/main.go` already declares a *local* mirror rather than importing `pricing.ModelRate` — so the seam is half-built. But it uses that one struct both to read the canonical response and to write the embedded files, so it needs a camelCase read shape and a snake_case write shape. Also decide whether its `-source` local-file mode follows the wire or the disk format.
- `table.go`, the embedded `models/*.json`, and settings: unchanged.
- Tests: ~9 fixture sites across `remote_refresh_test.go`, `settings_pricing_test.go`, `table_test.go`, plus pricingsync's own.

**entire.io — nothing.**

## Two things that make now the cheap moment

The endpoint 404s in production, so **no `schema_version` bump is needed** — nothing has ever consumed the snake_case shape. Ship it after deploy and the CLI has to accept both spellings forever.

And any stale `~/.cache/entire/pricing_remote.json` from someone testing the branch self-heals: the camelCase body deserializes to a zero-value `SchemaVersion`, fails the `!= 1` check, gets ignored, and the next refresh overwrites it. No migration needed.

Want me to do it? I'd do entire-api and the CLI as two commits on the existing branches and leave entire.io alone.

content.text:
Fair challenge — but there is a real reason, and it's in the config:

```jsonc
// entire-api's public pricing catalog (non-tenant; any cell serves
// the identical table). See routes/pricing.ts.
"ENTIRE_API_PRICING_BASE_URL": "https://aws-us-east-2.api.entire.io"
```

entire-api's canonical endpoint lives on a **jurisdictional cell hostname**. And `entire.io/api/v1/*` is already claimed by entire.io's own Worker, so entire-api isn't reachable at a bare-domain path either.

So without the proxy, the CLI's default `RemoteURL` has to hardcode `aws-us-east-2.api.entire.io`. That would pin every install worldwide to one US cell, break on any cell rename or retirement, send EU users' fetches to a US host, and bake cell topology into a shipped binary — which is exactly what the rest of the codebase works hard to keep behind discovery (`cluster_cores.json`, `api_discovery.json`, home-jurisdiction routing).

`entire.io/pricing/v1/models.json` is a **stable vendor-neutral alias over cell topology**. Same job `/.well-known/entire-api.json` already does on that zone. The edge cache is a secondary win — daily polls from every install collapse to a handful of origin fetches per PoP instead of hitting a cell directly.

## That said, your instinct is pointing at something real

For one static table, the proxy has already cost: an extra hop with its own 502 mode, a cross-repo deploy-order dependency, an immutable-headers crash at the edge (`e4e43872`), and another still-open finding about a Cache API rejection bypassing the fetch. Three repos in the chain for a file that changes when someone edits a rate.

The alternative that actually removes it is to give entire-api a **stable non-cell public alias** — `pricing.entire.io`, or a cell-agnostic `api.entire.io` — and point the CLI straight at it. The table is explicitly non-tenant, so there's no routing reason it needs to sit behind a cell hostname at all. Cloudflare still caches it at the edge; you just lose the Worker in the middle.

That's a DNS/routing change rather than an application one, which is why the proxy exists instead — it was the thing that could be built in the repo the author was already in.

**My read:** the proxy is justified *given* that entire-api has no stable public alias today. If you'd rather not carry a third repo in this chain long-term, the right fix is the alias, and then entire.io#3643 gets deleted rather than merged. Worth deciding before it ships, because once the CLI's default URL points at `entire.io/pricing/v1/`, moving it means a CLI release.

Either way it doesn't change the camelCase work — the proxy is a byte pass-through, so the endpoint whose casing is at issue is entire-api's regardless.

cache rates still serialize as null, not 0: Anthropic's entries

content.text:
Both PRs updated and pushed.

## entire-api — `e16c0c1eb`

Added a `pricingCatalogModel` wire DTO with camelCase tags (`schemaVersion`, `inputPerMTok`, `cacheWrite1hPerMTok`, …) plus a mapper from `pricing.ModelRate`. `internal/pricing`, the embedded JSON, and `pricingcheck` are untouched.

The camelCase guard test walks the **raw** response rather than a typed struct — a typed decode ignores unknown keys, which is exactly how a snake_case field would ship unnoticed. It caught something immediately: huma injects a `$schema` key into every response body. That's JSON Schema's prescribed spelling, so it falls under CASING-001's external-protocol carve-out and is excluded with a comment saying why.

Second test proves nil cache rates still serialize as `null`, not `0`. Anthropic's entries deliberately omit them so `Estimate` applies the 0.1×/1.25×/2× multipliers — a zeroed rate would tell consumers those tokens are free, which is the same class of silent mispricing that started all this.

Build, vet, `mise run lint` (0 issues), tests green.

## CLI — `a28f6b169`

Both readers of the canonical catalog needed the camelCase shape: the opt-in runtime refresh (`remote.go`) and the release-time export (`pricingsync`). Each gets a wire type plus a conversion.

**This mattered more than I expected.** Both were parsing the catalog with the same snake_case structs the embedded files use, so once entire-api flipped, every rate would have parsed as **zero** — and zero fails silently, not loudly. `validateRate` drops zero-rate entries, so the runtime refresh would have degraded quietly to embedded-only, and the weekly CI freshness gate would have reported "no drift" against a catalog it had actually failed to read. A green gate reporting on nothing.

So I added a test pinning both directions: camelCase parses with every field populated, and snake_case does **not** silently parse as zeroes, with `validateCatalog` as the backstop that makes it a hard failure. Catalog fixtures moved to a separate `writeCatalog` helper so confusing wire shape with file shape fails loudly.

`mise run check` green — fmt, lint, unit, integration, Vogon canary (4/4).

## What I deliberately didn't touch

`pricing.ModelRate`'s tags, the embedded `models/*.json`, and the on-disk refresh cache at `~/.cache/entire/pricing_remote.json`. The first two are a storage format shared with the user-facing `pricing.models` override block in `.entire/settings.json` — re-casing would silently invalidate every existing user override file. The cache is a local artifact, so leaving it snake_case means caches written by earlier builds still parse and no migration is needed.

entire.io needed nothing, as expected — its proxy parses to `unknown` and passes bytes through.

No `schema_version` bump anywhere: the endpoint still 404s in production, so nothing has ever consumed the snake_case shape.

Two things still outstanding from earlier, unchanged: the six CASING-001 findings on trail 298 (still yours to call), and the merge-order constraint — entire-api before entire.io before any CLI release that ships `pricing:sync`.
can you resolve/reject the findings on the trail?

Done. Here's where trail 298 stands.

## Dismissed — 11 CASING-001 findings

All additive fields on pre-existing snake_case shapes, dismissed under the rule you set: **new endpoints and new response surfaces must be camelCase; fields joining an existing shape must match that shape.**

The `ProjectSpend` one was the closest call, and the finding's premise was factually correct — it *is* a new type, absent from main. But it's embedded under `project_spend` inside the existing checkpoint-metrics body, next to `checkpoint_count`. CamelCasing its interior gives you `{"checkpoint_count": 1, "project_spend": {"projectId": ...}}` — mixed casing in one document. So it's the additive case at object granularity. I noted in the dismissal that if project spend ever gets its own endpoint, that surface would be new and should be camelCase.

Each dismissal records the reasoning and points at the amendment, so this doesn't read as tidying away signal.

## Fixed — SEC-002 was a real gap in my own commit

The review caught something I got wrong. `registerPricingCatalog` set neither `Security` nor `Middlewares` and relied on a comment. The convention here is that ops declare **both** axes — authed ones set `Security: secSchemes, Middlewares: mw`, and `runner_issuer.go`'s public discovery/JWKS ops set `Security: public`.

There's no document-level security default, so the route was already public at runtime — but the OpenAPI doc couldn't distinguish "deliberately open" from "forgot the auth". That matters more than usual here, since entire.io's credential-less Worker depends on that contract. Fixed and pushed as `8a34daf74`; lint clean, tests green.

## Left open deliberately — three that need you

**NAME-001** (Medium) — "cost in USD" is spelled three ways across this PR: bare `cost` in recap types, `costUsd` in checkpoint/session/transcript types, `cost_usd` in team rollups. That's a genuine cross-API naming inconsistency, not a false positive, and picking one is a design decision spanning surfaces I shouldn't unilaterally rename.

**PATH-001** (Medium) — `/pricing/models.json` has a non-kebab-case segment because of the `.json` suffix. Defensible as a file-like static artifact (mirroring `/.well-known/entire-api.json` on the same zone), but it isn't a `.well-known` path. Changing it is cheap *now* and requires a coordinated entire.io edit — same free-window logic as the casing change.

**Three UNIT-001 findings** flagging bare `cost` / `avg_cost_per_checkpoint` as currency fields without a unit suffix. Related to NAME-001; probably worth deciding together.

Plus four substantive technical findings from others still open (`UpsertMyActivity` cost columns on the phase+sequence gate, `costSourceAgg`'s `min()`, `projectSpend` authz, and the older store one). I haven't verified those as fixed, so I left them alone rather than guess.

Checked both rules. You're right on PATH-001, and the `cost` question has a cleaner answer than I gave you.

## PATH-001 — the finding is misfiled

```yaml
rule: Entire-defined path segments are kebab-case, collections are plural
      nouns, and paths contain no verbs; ...
signal: static Entire-defined path segments match ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$
```

`models.json` satisfies every **normative** clause: lowercase, plural noun, no verb. There is no word boundary anywhere in it — nothing to hyphenate. The regex fails on exactly one character: the `.`.

So "non-kebab-case segment" is the wrong description of the problem. The signal is a *proxy* for kebab-case and it's tripping on an unrelated character class.

There is a real question underneath — should a path segment carry a file extension at all — but that's not PATH-001, and it's arguable both ways: `.json` reads as a static cacheable artifact, which is exactly what this is, and it matches `/.well-known/entire-api.json` on the same zone (not under the carve-out, but the same instinct). I'd dismiss it as misfiled and note the extension question separately if you want it considered on its merits.

## `cost` vs `costUsd` — UNIT-001 doesn't actually ask for this

```yaml
- id: UNIT-001
  level: SHOULD
  rule: Numeric durations and counts carry their unit in the name.
  signal: duration fields end Ms/Seconds; token counts end Tokens
```

It's a **SHOULD**, and it's scoped to **durations and counts**. It says nothing about currency. So the three UNIT-001 findings flagging bare `cost` are stretching a rule about milliseconds and token counts to cover money. Your instinct is backed by the rule text — nothing mandates the `Usd` suffix.

The binding rule is **NAME-001** (one concept, one name), and that one is unarguable: three spellings for the same value is wrong whichever you pick.

**My recommendation is still `costUsd`**, but for a different reason than the linter gives:

The storage layer already decided. It's `cost_usd NUMERIC(14,6)` in Postgres, `CostUSD` in entire-api's Go, and `CostUSD` in the CLI's `types.TokenUsage`. Bare `cost` on the wire is the outlier in its own stack. Aligning the wire to the column means zero renames anywhere below the API, and `cost: 3.2` is genuinely ambiguous at a glance — dollars, cents, credits?

One thing to write into that decision explicitly, or it'll collide with what we just settled: **"one name" means one name, cased per surface** — `costUsd` on camelCase surfaces, `cost_usd` on snake_case ones. Not one literal string everywhere. Without that sentence someone will read NAME-001 as licence to camelCase the team rollups we just dismissed.

Want me to dismiss PATH-001 and the three UNIT-001s as misapplied, and leave NAME-001 open with that clarification in a comment? The `cost` → `costUsd` rename itself spans recap and me/summary surfaces, so I'd want you to confirm before touching those.

content.text:
`costUsd` is done and pushed — `b0785f28a`. Now your path question, which turns out to be right but about a different URL than the finding is aimed at.

## The rename

Four bare `cost` fields, cased per surface as we agreed:

| Site | Family | New key |
|---|---|---|
| `me_types.go` `meAgentAggregate`, `meSummaryTotals` | camelCase (`agentId`, `filesChanged`, `toolMix`) | `costUsd` |
| `types.go` `RecapAgent`, `RecapOutput.Summary` | snake_case (`files_changed`, `active_days`, `repo_count`) | `cost_usd` |

All four are new in this PR — absent from main — so nothing consumes them and entire.io needed no coordination. Build, vet, lint (0 issues), full `./internal/...` suite green.

**One thing I overrode, so you know it happened:** `types.go` carried an explicit comment arguing bare `cost` was deliberate, paralleling the recap family's bare aggregates (`tokens`, `checkpoints`, `sessions`). I replaced it, because the parallel doesn't hold — `tokens` already carries its unit *in the name*, which is exactly what makes it unambiguous and exactly what bare `cost` lacks. And the storage layer had already settled it: `cost_usd` in Postgres, `CostUSD` in both Go codebases.

Also resolved NAME-001 and dismissed the three UNIT-001s — as you suspected, UNIT-001 is a **SHOULD** scoped to "durations and counts", silent on currency. It never compelled the suffix. NAME-001 did.

## On `/.pricing/models.json`

Your instinct is right, but it applies to the **other** URL. There are two paths here and they don't have to match:

- **entire-api**: `/api/v1/pricing/models.json` — internal plumbing. The CLI never sees it; only entire.io's `new URL(...)` line references it. Inside a versioned API namespace, it isn't polluting anything.
- **entire.io**: `/pricing/v1/models.json` — on the apex marketing domain, carved out of the frontend worker's catch-all. `https://entire.io/pricing` currently returns a **307**, so there's already a marketing route there. A JSON API sitting underneath a marketing page's namespace is the real collision, and it's the URL the CLI hardcodes.

On the leading-dot form specifically, I'd avoid it: RFC 8615 reserves `/.well-known/` and nothing else. Inventing `/.pricing/` borrows the *appearance* of a registered convention without the substance — and it wouldn't even satisfy the linter, since PATH-001's signal is `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$` and a leading `.` fails it exactly like `.json` does. Its only exemption is the `.well-known` subtree.

So the two options that actually work:

**Cleanest for entire-api** — `/api/v1/pricing/models`. Plain resource, fully PATH-001 conformant, already versioned by `/v1/`, JSON via the `Accept` header the CLI already sends.

**If you want it out of the marketing namespace on entire.io** — `entire.io/.well-known/entire-pricing.json`. That's the genuine reserved subtree, gets the actual carve-out, and there's direct precedent on that exact zone: `entire.io/.well-known/entire-api.json` is already carved out the same way.

Both are still free — nothing is deployed, and the CLI's default `RemoteURL` is a one-line change until a release ships with it. Want me to do either? I'd leave PATH-001 open until you decide, since the finding as written is misfiled but the question under it is now a live one.

I like it. It's the most honest description of what this actually is — one static file — and it has better precedent than anything we've discussed: `robots.txt`, `security.txt`, `sitemap.xml` all live at apex root for exactly this reason.

It also sidesteps the marketing-namespace collision cleanly, rather than nesting a JSON API under a route that already 307s.

## Two things to be clear about before you commit to it

**It doesn't resolve PATH-001.** That finding is against `internal/httpapi/pricing_catalog.go:97` — *entire-api's* path, `/api/v1/pricing/models.json`. The rule lives in entire-api's `.entire/runners/api-design-rules.yaml` and has never governed entire.io's Worker routes. So these are two independent decisions:

- entire.io public URL → `entire.io/model-pricing.json` (your call, good one)
- entire-api internal path → still `/api/v1/pricing/models.json`, still flagged, and I'd still go `/api/v1/pricing/models` there

**You'd be dropping the version from the path.** Today it's `/pricing/v1/models.json`; `model-pricing.json` has no `v1`. The only version signal becomes `schemaVersion` in the body.

I think that's fine, and arguably better — the CLI already hard-rejects `SchemaVersion != 1` and degrades to embedded defaults, so the body is doing the real work and the path segment is decorative. A future breaking change becomes `model-pricing-v2.json`, which is more legible than a silently-reinterpreted `/v1/` prefix. But it's a deliberate trade and worth stating rather than discovering later.

## Scope

Genuinely small — about ten lines:

- **CLI**: 3 references (`RemoteURL` in `remote.go`, `defaultSource` + a doc comment in `pricingsync/main.go`)
- **entire.io**: 2 wrangler route patterns (prod `entire.io` + staging `partial.to`), the `app.route("/pricing", …)` mount, the handler path, and a few doc comments

Still free — nothing is deployed and no CLI release ships the URL yet. This is the last cheap window for the same reason the casing change was.

Want me to do it? I'd make it one commit per repo, and separately switch entire-api to `/api/v1/pricing/models` so PATH-001 closes properly — unless you'd rather keep the `.json` suffix there too, in which case I'll dismiss PATH-001 as a deliberate call instead.

fix(pricing): drop the .json suffix from the catalog path (PATH-001)

PATH-001 requires Entire-defined path segments to match
^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$; "models.json" failed it on the literal dot. The rule's
only exemption is the reserved .well-known subtree, which this is not.

The finding described it as a kebab-case violation, which was a
mischaracterization worth noting: "models" is already lowercase, already
plural, and not a verb — it satisfies every normative clause of the rule,
and there is no word boundary anywhere in the segment that kebab-case
would address. The regex trips on one character. The real question was
whether a path segment should carry a file extension at all, and the
answer here is no: the media type is negotiated via Accept (the CLI
already sends application/json), so encoding it in the path is redundant.

  GET /api/v1/pricing/models.json  ->  GET /api/v1/pricing/models

entire.io's public mirror moves the other way in a separate change — it
becomes the literal single file entire.io/model-pricing.json, where a
suffix is honest about what it is (robots.txt / sitemap.xml precedent)
and where PATH-001 does not apply, since that route is a Cloudflare
Worker on the marketing zone rather than an Entire-defined API path.
Two surfaces, two conventions, deliberately.

Free to change: the endpoint is not deployed (it 404s in production) and
the only consumer is entire.io's proxy, updated in lockstep.

content.text:
All three shipped. Clones are back on their original branches.

| Repo | Commit | Change |
|---|---|---|
| entire-api | `045d72312` | `/api/v1/pricing/models.json` → `/api/v1/pricing/models` |
| entire.io | `cf6652d2cf` | `/pricing/v1/models.json` → `/model-pricing.json`, upstream follows |
| CLI | `93c0b5c9e` | `RemoteURL` + `pricingsync` `defaultSource` → `entire.io/model-pricing.json` |

Verification: entire-api build/vet/lint clean, tests green. entire.io 13 pricing tests updated across **both** describe blocks — I initially missed the `createPricingRoutes` edge-cache block, which uses bare `/v1/models.json` because it mounts the router directly; full suite 146 files / 2442 tests, `tsc` and `oxlint` clean. CLI `mise run check` green including canary 56/56 and 4/4.

Two things worth knowing:

**No cache migration needed on the CLI.** The on-disk refresh cache records `SourceURL`, and `cacheStillFresh` already treats a source mismatch as stale — so a cache written against the old URL is refetched rather than served under the new URL's name. That guard was added for `ENTIRE_PRICING_URL` overrides and happens to cover this exactly.

**PATH-001 is resolved — and my change immediately triggered a new finding.** Dropping `.json` made the path read as a REST *collection*, so `PAGE-001`/`PAGE-003` now fire: no `pageSize`/`pageToken`, no `{items, nextPageToken}` envelope.

I should own that trade honestly: the `.json` suffix was doing real work by signalling "document, fetch whole" rather than "browsable collection", and reverting is a coherent position.

But I don't think we should revert, because **pagination here would be actively harmful**. The CLI builds its entire `Table` from this response; a partial fetch produces a table missing models, `Lookup` misses, and cost comes back nil — silent underpricing, which is the exact failure class this whole workstream exists to eliminate. It's also bounded reference data (218 entries, ~57 KB, capped by how many models exist), cached 1h at the edge and 24h in the CLI. And an `{items, nextPageToken}` envelope would break the schema shared with the CLI's `fileSchema` and entire.io, forcing a `schemaVersion` bump across three repos for no benefit.

The finding itself offers the right out — *"If this catalog is meant to be exempt from pagination as bounded reference data, that should be a stated exemption."* So I'd state the exemption in the operation doc and dismiss it on that basis, rather than revert.

Want me to do that? It's a couple of lines in `pricing_catalog.go` plus the dismissal.
